before: A w:br or w:cr written directly under a paragraph or hyperlink, outside a run, was typed as a hard break. That child failed its container's content check, so the whole paragraph (or link) was read as a generic node and its text left the layout and the editable flow.
after: The reader types w:br and w:cr as hard breaks only inside a WML run. Under any other WML parent they stay generic at their position, so the paragraph and its runs stay typed. Breaks inside runs and breaks under non-WML parents are typed as before.
reason: This is an import-side typing rule over OOXML bytes. Shared state stores each element's kind as seeded, and materialization reads that stored kind, so a room keeps the structure its seeding participant wrote. A typed paragraph with a generic child is a structure released participants already store, materialize, lay out, and edit. No stored field, operation kind, identity rule, or repair rule changes.
